events: The Holy Club
At Oxford a small society kept by Charles Wesley and soon led by John is mocked as the Holy Club and the Methodists.
Georgia
John and Charles Wesley sail with the colony of Georgia. John prints a book of psalms and hymns at Charles-Town in 1737.
Aldersgate Street
On 24 May John Wesley finds his heart strangely warmed at a society meeting in London.
Into the fields
Whitefield preaches to the colliers of Kingswood. Wesley follows at Bristol on 2 April. In London an old foundry becomes Wesley’s chapel.
The Awakening
Whitefield preaches from Georgia to New England. Philadelphia and Boston print his sermons and journals as fast as he writes them.
Free grace
Wesley’s sermon against predestination and Whitefield’s answer part the revival into Arminian and Calvinistic Methodists.
The first Conference
Wesley’s preachers meet at the Foundery in June. Their Minutes become the rule of the connexion.
The New Testament notes
Explanatory Notes upon the New Testament. The Old Testament follows from Bristol in 1765.
Newburyport
Whitefield dies in Massachusetts on 30 September. The Conference Minutes of the same year reopen the quarrel over grace. Fletcher answers with his Checks.
Asbury sails
Francis Asbury leaves for America and never returns.
The hymnbook
A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists.
A church in America
The Deed of Declaration gives the Conference its legal being. Wesley ordains preachers for America. At Christmas the Methodist Episcopal Church is formed at Baltimore.
Wesley dies
John Wesley dies in London on 2 March. His brother had died three years before.
The Plan of Pacification
Where a society wishes it, its preachers may give the sacraments. The Methodists become a church of their own.
Asbury dies
Asbury dies in Virginia. The church he led has spread west over the mountains.
North and South
The Methodist Episcopal Church divides over slavery. The Methodist Episcopal Church, South, is organized the next year.
The Works
Jackson’s third edition of Wesley’s Works is the edition the shelf holds.
